conventions.independent_variable: volume-average (bare) time t, in 'HT' units where the dressed H_0 = 1; GyrstoHT = h/9.778 with h = 0.7323 (notebook) / 0.7303 (paper values)
conventions.derivative: overdot = d/dt along the dust frame (n^mu nabla_mu); notebook systems are dv/dt = A(t) v
conventions.scale_factor: a(t) = a_D(t), volume-average scale factor, normalised so a_w,0 = 1, hence a_D(t0) = a0 = 1 + f_v0/2 = 1.3685 (NOT 1)
conventions.expansion_perturbation: Z := a D^mu (a D_mu Theta), so row 1 gives dDelta_d/dt = -Z, i.e. Z = -dDelta_d/dt
conventions.units_of_k: 1/HL with HL = 3000/h Mpc (h = 0.7323 in the Timescape notebook); see finding F7 for the normalisation discrepancy vs the paper caption
conventions.solver: scipy.integrate.solve_ivp with ALL defaults (RK45, rtol=1e-3, atol=1e-6); t_eval = linspace(0.218*GyrstoHT, t0, 1000)

provenance.recipe: ic[0] = 6.6e-2 * qplus(20); ic[1] = -6.6e-2 * qplus_dot(20), where qplus is the closed-form flat-LCDM growing mode D+(z) (incomplete-beta form) with Omega_m = 0.315, Omega_L = 0.685, H0 = 1 (h = 0.674 time units), qplus_prime the forward finite difference with eps = 1e-5, and qplus_dot = qplus_prime * (-(1+z) H(z)). Exact float64 equality with both upstream values. Source code of the recipe: ACPT_RZA.ipynb cells 2-4 and 16; identical hard-coded values in ACPT_GMC.ipynb cell 19.
provenance.paper_consistency: 6.6e-2*qplus(1090) = 6.049e-5, matching the paper's 'typical amplitude 6e-5 at the CMB epoch' (Sec. 5.1.2); qplus(20)/qplus(1100) = 52.43 (growth from CMB to z=20).

initial_conditions.z_ic_sign_convention: Z(t_i) = -dDelta_d/dt(t_i) < 0 for a growing mode; Meszaros solver flips it back (ic_new = [ic[0], -ic[1]]). VERIFIED consistent across all four notebooks (RZA/GMC additionally divide by dz/dt for z-space integration).

unit_question.detail: ic[1] is numerically -0.169741 in units of H0_LCDM (h = 0.674) but is injected unchanged into the Timescape notebook whose time unit is 1/H0_dressed (h = 0.7323). The unit-consistent value would be -0.169741 * (0.674/0.7323) = -0.156227. The paper's own text 'Z(t_i) ~ -0.16 H0' matches the CONVERTED value (-0.156 rounds to -0.16) better than the value actually used (-0.170). Magnitude of the injected initial contraction rate is therefore 8.65% larger than the LCDM-matched physical rate under the conversion reading.

initial_conditions.delta_eff_and_tilt: Delta_eff(t_i) = 0 and Vtilde_eff(t_i) = 0 stated explicitly in Sec. 5.1.2; V_eff = Vtilde_eff/(1+w_eff) = 0 equivalently (1+w_eff(t_i)) = 0.507 != 0.

findings.confirmed_fact: Eqs. (4.10)+(4.13) imply the Delta_eff coefficient (w_eff - cs2_eff)*Theta, while printed Eq. (4.15) [and hence (4.19), Appendix A, and ALL FOUR notebooks' A33] uses (w_eff + cs2_eff)*Theta; symbolic residual exactly 2*cs2*Theta*Delta_eff. The Meszaros-section Eq. (4.29) is sympy-verified to sit on the (4.10) branch (exact match; the (4.15)-branch derivation fails). Every sign involved was double-extracted with two independent PDF tools. Numerical impact on A33 at early times: (w+c2) = -0.992 vs (w-c2) = +0.007; at t0: -0.765 vs +0.018.

findings.summary: t_i = 0.218 Gyr (cells 15-19) does not correspond to z = 20 under any tested definition (dressed z = 18.59 there; dressed z = 20 is at 0.19620 Gyr). Provenance unexplained.

Printed (2.12) has '-2*Lambda' where the standard Raychaudhuri (and the paper's own derived (4.19)/(4.25)/(4.26), sympy-verified) require '-Lambda'; printed (2.13) has '-2*Lambda' where the standard Hamiltonian constraint requires '+2*Lambda'; the printed pair is mutually inconsistent for Lambda != 0 (consistency demands the (2.13) coefficient equal twice the (2.12) coefficient with matching sign). No effect on any Timescape (Lambda=0) result and no effect on GMC/GMP numerics (Lambda enters only their backgrounds, computed independently).
Published Fig. 3 right panel plots Delta_eff/k^2 (y-range 1e-5..1e0); notebook cell 19 plots raw Delta_eff (y-range 1e-4..1e0).

Wavenumber normalisation: paper caption's 'k in LCDM H0/c units, k=2pi = horizon' is exactly realised only in RZA/GMC (a0=1, h=0.674). In the Timescape notebook the same k values act on k^2/a_D^2 with a_D,0 = 1.3685 and h = 0.7323, so the k=2pi mode has present-day physical wavelength 1.26 x c/H0_LCDM.
